Harvard Management Company.desc: The company that manages and invests Harvard University's endowment, largely through outside managers. The endowment it oversees was worth $56.9 billion at the end of Harvard's 2025 fiscal year, on 30 June 2025.

sources.title: Harvard's Endowment, Donations Rise-but the University Runs a Deficit

Hellas Gold S.A. (Eldorado Gold).desc: Hellas Gold Single Member S.A. is the Eldorado Gold subsidiary that holds Eldorado's operating assets in Greece and the Skouries project. Its parent, Eldorado Gold Corporation, is a gold miner governed by the Canada Business Corporations Act with mines in Turkiye, Canada and Greece, listed as ELD on the Toronto Stock Exchange and EGO on the New York Stock Exchange; Eldorado produced 520,293 ounces of gold and directly employed 5,884 employees and contractors worldwide in 2024.

sources.title: Eldorado Gold Corporation Annual Information Form (EX-99.1 to Form 40-F)

Hengfu Group Sugar Industry Co., Ltd..desc: A Chinese-owned sugar business. Five companies granted economic land concessions in Cambodia's Preah Vihear province in 2011, covering 40,000 hectares for sugarcane production, are believed to be subsidiaries of it; one of them, Rui Feng, built a sugar refinery reported to have cost US$360 million that media reports say was never operational, and in February 2020 it was reported that the Hengfu companies had shut down their entire operation.

sources.title: Goodbye Hengfu

Hengfu Group Sugar Industry Co., Ltd..note: No company register entry, named owner or size figure for Hengfu Group Sugar Industry Co., Ltd. was found on an accessible source; the report names the firm only as 'Hengfu'.

Herakles Farms.desc: A US company, formally Herakles Farms LLC, registered in Delaware, which owns 100 percent of the Cameroonian palm oil company SG Sustainable Oils Cameroon (SGSOC). It is an affiliate of Herakles Capital, an Africa-focused private investment firm involved in the telecommunications, energy, infrastructure, mining and agro-industrial sectors; Bruce Wrobel was its chairman and chief executive. Ownership of SGSOC was transferred from Sithe Global, a Blackstone Group company, to Herakles Capital in 2009.

sources.title: Understanding Land Investment Deals in Africa: Herakles Farms in Cameroon (land deal brief)

Hidalgo e Hidalgo.desc: An Ecuadorian construction firm founded in 1969 with operations in Ecuador, specialising in road works, bridges, ports, sanitation works, electrification, irrigation and buildings. No published revenue, employee figure or shareholder list was found.

sources.title: Hidalgo e Hidalgo S.A. (HeH Constructores) company profile

Hidro Salá S.A..desc: A Guatemalan power company that operates the proposed 15 MW Rio Sala hydroelectric project on the Sala River in San Pablo, San Marcos, for which the government issued it a 50-year operating contract in February 2011. It is part of the FABRIGAS group: another FABRIGAS company, Generadores Electricos S.A. (Genhidro), was its majority shareholder and administrator, and in March 2016 Genhidro opted not to pursue the project and sold its holding to FABRIGAS, described as Genhidro and Hidro Sala's mutual parent company.

sources.title: Case 4: Rio Sala, Guatemala
sources.publisher: Coalition for Human Rights in Development

Hidrovias do Brasil.desc: A Brazilian logistics company focused on waterway transport, moving cargo by barge; it operates four port terminals with a combined loading capacity of 20.5 million tonnes a year, a transshipment station, 476 cargo barges and 28 tugboats (22 main and 6 auxiliary). It is listed on Brazil's B3 exchange as HBSA3 in the Novo Mercado segment and reported consolidated net revenue of R$802.2 million in the first half of 2024.

sources.title: Earnings release, second quarter 2024

Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd (.desc: An Indian state power generation company incorporated in 2006 to handle power generation on behalf of the Himachal Pradesh government and the Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB), which hold 60% and 40% respectively and are its major shareholders. As of March 2018 it had an operating portfolio of 295 MW, including three hydro projects.

sources.title: HPPCL: Emerging as a key hydro player in Himachal Pradesh

Hindalco.desc: Hindalco Industries Limited is the metals flagship of India's Aditya Birla Group, described as India's largest fully integrated aluminium player, with a copper business and a specialty alumina business, and it wholly owns Novelis, the world's largest producer of flat-rolled aluminium and aluminium recycler. Revenue was Rs 238,496 crore in the 2024-25 financial year.

sources.title: Hindalco at a Glance, Integrated Annual Report 2024-25

Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Pvt Ltd.desc: An unlisted soft-drink bottling company, described as the bottling arm of Coca-Cola in India, operating 16 factories across India. Revenue from operations was Rs 14,021.54 crore in the 2023-24 financial year.

Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Pvt. Ltd..desc: An unlisted soft-drink bottling company, described as the bottling arm of Coca-Cola in India, operating 16 factories across India. Revenue from operations was Rs 14,021.54 crore in the 2023-24 financial year.

sources.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages FY24 profit jumps three-fold to Rs 2,808 cr; revenue rises 10 pc

Hindustan Unilever Ltd (formerly Ponds /.desc: An Indian consumer-goods maker incorporated in 1933 that makes soaps, detergents, cosmetics, toiletries and packaged foods, listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India, with Unilever PLC listed as its holding company. Turnover was Rs 61,517 crore in the 2024-25 financial year, with 8,202 employees and 18,465 workers.

sources.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report FY 2024-25, Section A

Hoang Anh Gia Lai (HAGL), via Hoang Anh.desc: A Vietnamese agricultural company with its head office in Pleiku City, Gia Lai Province, listed on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange since 15 December 2008 under the code HAG; it grows bananas and durians and raises banana-fed pigs, and its history records completing the planting of 50,000 hectares of rubber trees in 2012. Consolidated net revenue was VND 5,783 billion in 2024, with 1,756 employees on long-term contracts at the end of that year and a direct workforce at its farms in Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia reaching 10 thousand people.

sources.title: Annual Report 2024, Hoang Anh Gia Lai Joint Stock Company
sources.publisher: Hoang Anh Gia Lai JSC (filed via Vietstock)

Huaneng Shandong Ruyi (Pakistan) Energy.desc: Huaneng Shandong Ruyi (Pakistan) Energy (Private) Limited is a power company registered under Pakistan's Companies Ordinance 1984, with a corporate universal identification number dated 28 May 2014 and its office in Lahore; its letter of intent went to 'Huaneng Shandong Ruyi a group of People Republic of China'. Its generation licence covers a thermal plant of two 660 MW supercritical units at Qadirabad, Sahiwal, in Punjab, burning imported lignite or bituminous coal, with an installed capacity of 1,320 MW gross and 1,227 MW net.

sources.title: Generation Licence No. LAG-292, Huaneng Shandong Ruyi (Pakistan) Energy (Private) Limited
sources.publisher: National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA), Pakistan

Hunan Gold Group.desc: A Chinese limited liability company, locally state-owned controlled, whose business is the investment, development and use of mineral resources such as gold, nonferrous metals, rare earth metals and non-metallic minerals and the production and sale of related products, along with capital operation and management and mining, beneficiation and smelting technology research. Established on 13 April 2006, it is the direct controlling shareholder of the Shenzhen-listed Hunan Gold Corporation Limited, holding 35.98% of its shares at the end of 2023; Hunan Nonferrous is named as the listed company's indirect controlling shareholder.

sources.title: Hunan Gold Corporation Limited Annual Report 2023

Hunt Oil.desc: An oil company incorporated in Delaware on 18 December 1934, founded by H.L. Hunt, which moved to Dallas in 1937 from its first office in Tyler, Texas; its recorded work is oil field discovery, drilling and production. It is one of the Hunt Family of Companies, which are serviced by Hunt Consolidated, Inc. No published revenue or employee figure was found.

sources.title: Our History

Hydro-Québec International and Elyo (con.desc: Elyo was an energy services business within GDF SUEZ's Energy Services business line; in the United Kingdom and France the new Cofely name replaced the Elyo and Cofathec names with immediate effect in March 2009, as GDF SUEZ brought its energy services activities under one brand. Contemporary accounts of the consortium call the pairing of Elyo and Hydroquebec International a Franco-Canadian company.

Hydroproject Institute.desc: A Moscow-based design and research institute, formally the Design and Research Institute Hydroproject, named after S.Y. Zhuk, founded in 1930, which specialises in the design of hydropower facilities and has branches in other Russian cities. With its predecessors and branches it has built over 250 hydropower projects totalling 65 GW of installed capacity, 45 GW of it in Russia; RusHydro Group purchased 100% of it through its wholly owned subsidiary JSC Gidroinvest, reported in October 2010.

sources.title: RusHydro Group concludes acquisition of Hydroproject Institute

Hyundai Motor Company.desc: South Korea's top automaker, which makes and sells cars. Revenue was a record 175.2 trillion Korean won in 2024, on global sales of 4.14 million vehicles.

IAMGOLD.desc: A gold mining company organized under the Canada Business Corporations Act with its head office in Toronto, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (IAG) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (IMG). It operates the Cote Gold and Westwood mines in Canada and the Essakane mine in Burkina Faso, and employed 3,705 people as at 20 March 2025.

sources.title: Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2024

IEnova / Gasoducto de Aguaprieta.desc: Infraestructura Energetica Nova, S.A.B. de C.V. (IEnova) develops, builds and operates energy infrastructure in Mexico, including natural gas and renewables infrastructure, and was the first energy infrastructure company to be listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange. It had more than 1,400 employees and about US$10.5 billion of total assets at the end of 2020; its parent Sempra Energy offered in 2021 to exchange the IEnova shares it did not already own, and the Mexican exchange's issuer record for IENOVA now shows its series as cancelled.

IOI Corporation.desc: An oil palm plantation company whose plantation business operates across Malaysia and Indonesia, with a total oil palm planted area of 167,883 hectares in its 2025 financial year and crude palm oil mill production of 616,307 tonnes that year. It reported revenue of RM9.60 billion in its Annual Report 2024.

sources.title: Integrated Report 2025, Plantation section
Integrated Report 2024, Highlights of the Year

ISAGEN.desc: A Colombian power generation company that owns and operates a 3,032 MW portfolio, consisting predominantly of six largely reservoir-based hydroelectric facilities, with annual generation expected to approximate 15,000 GWh; it is described as Colombia's third-largest power generation company. A consortium of Brookfield Renewable and its institutional partners acquired an initial 57.6% interest in it from the Colombian government, with an acquisition date of 22 January 2016.

Iamgold Corporation.desc: A gold mining company organized under the Canada Business Corporations Act with its head office in Toronto, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (IAG) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (IMG). It operates the Cote Gold and Westwood mines in Canada and the Essakane mine in Burkina Faso, and employed 3,705 people as at 20 March 2025.

sources.title: Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2024

Impregilo (Salini Impregilo).desc: An Italian construction group that builds large infrastructure, formed by combining Salini Impregilo with Astaldi. Salini Impregilo S.p.A. was renamed Webuild S.p.A. with effect from 15 May 2020, following the shareholders' resolution of 4 May 2020; the Webuild group was reported in 2020 as having 70,000 direct and indirect employees globally.

Salini Impregilo becomes Webuild

Indonesia Tourism Development Corporatio.desc: An Indonesian company, legally PT Pengembangan Pariwisata Indonesia (Persero), that focuses on the development and management of integrated tourism areas: The Nusa Dua in Bali, The Mandalika in Central Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara, and The Golo Mori in West Manggarai Regency, East Nusa Tenggara. It sits within PT Aviasi Pariwisata Indonesia (Persero), or InJourney, described as a holding ecosystem of state-owned enterprises, under Indonesian Government Regulations No. 72 and No. 104 of 2021, and it presents itself as InJourney Tourism Development Corporation; The Mandalika has an area of 1,175 hectares and has been a Special Economic Zone since 2017.

sources.title: About ITDC

Indorama Agro LLC.desc: A cotton farming and ginning business in Uzbekistan and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indorama Corporation. An IFC investment announced in 2021 financed about 50,000 hectares of farmland in the Syrdarya and Qashqadarya regions of Uzbekistan and support for independent farmers through contract farming.

sources.title: IFC Invests in Indorama Agro to Promote Sustainable Cotton in Uzbekistan

Indorama Group.desc: Indorama Corporation is described as one of Asia's leading chemical holding companies, based in Singapore, with products including nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, textiles, cotton fibre and medical gloves. It had over 20 manufacturing sites in eight countries and employed over 18,000 people worldwide as reported in 2021.

sources.title: IFC Invests in Indorama Agro to Promote Sustainable Cotton in Uzbekistan

Industrial Development Corporation of So.desc: A South African development finance institution established in 1940 through an Act of Parliament, the Industrial Development Corporation Act 22 of 1940, and fully owned by the South African Government. It funds industrial capacity and enterprise development from income on loans and equity stakes, exits from mature investments and borrowing, with a core focus on South Africa and a mandate extended in the 1990s to the rest of Africa, and it owns the Small Enterprise Finance Agency (Sefa).

sources.title: About Us
sources.publisher: Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa

Industrias Infinito S.A..desc: A company formerly named Placer Dome de Costa Rica, S.A., which under that name was a subsidiary of the Canadian mining company Placer Dome International. In 1998 it was sold to Lyon Lake Mines, Ltd. and its name was changed to Industrias Infinito S.A.; it requested an exploitation concession to develop a surface gold mine at Las Crucitas, and in May 2000 it was acquired by Vannessa Ventures Ltd., which later became Infinito Gold Ltd.

sources.title: Infinito Gold Ltd. v. Republic of Costa Rica, Decision on Jurisdiction (ICSID Case No. ARB/14/5)

Infinito Gold Ltd.desc: A company incorporated under the laws of the Province of British Columbia, Canada, previously known as Vannessa Ventures Ltd. Under that name it acquired Industrias Infinito in May 2000; its ICSID claim concerned the development of a gold mining project in the area of Las Crucitas. No published revenue or employee figure was found.

sources.title: Infinito Gold Ltd. v. Republic of Costa Rica, Decision on Jurisdiction (ICSID Case No. ARB/14/5)

Infrastructure Development Finance Compa.desc: An Indian finance company incorporated on 30 January 1997 as a public limited company at Chennai to act as a specialized financial intermediary for funding infrastructure projects, registered with the Reserve Bank of India as a non-banking finance company in 1998 and listed on the NSE and BSE in August 2005. Its name was changed to IDFC Limited with effect from 20 July 2012, its financing undertaking was demerged into IDFC Bank in 2014, and it merged into IDFC FIRST Bank in 2023.

sources.title: IDFC Ltd (merged) company summary

Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad.desc: Costa Rica's state electricity and telecommunications body, an autonomous public institution created by Law No. 449 of 8 April 1949 to meet national electricity demand and develop the country's energy sources, especially its water resources; telephone communications were added by Law No. 3226 of 28 October 1963. It heads the Grupo ICE, whose companies include CNFL, RACSA and CRICSA.

sources.publisher: Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad (published via El Observador CR)

Inter RAO.desc: A Russian energy holding company that generates and sells electricity and heat and is the country's only electricity importer and exporter. Reported shareholders at the end of 2023 included Rosneftegaz, its principal shareholder, with 26.37% and Inter RAO Capital with 29.56%; group electricity output was 97.18 billion kWh in the first nine months of 2024.

sources.title: Inter RAO power generation rises 5.9% in Jan-Sept 2024

International Group of Entrepreneurs (IG.desc: One of the biggest conglomerates in Myanmar, formally International Group of Entrepreneur Co. Ltd., set up in 1999; its first entity, Aung Yee Phyo Company, was founded in 1994 by Aung Thaung, then a deputy commerce minister, with his wife and three sons on its board. Aung Thaung's son Nay Aung chairs it, and he and his business partner Win Kyaing are named as co-founders; its interests include timber export, oil and gas field operation, telecommunications, power generation and hotels. The EU sanctioned it in February 2022.

sources.title: Children of Notorious Ex-Myanmar Junta Minister Continue Corrupt Legacy

International Water Services (Guayaquil).desc: The private company that operates all water and wastewater facilities and systems in the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador, under a 30-year concession from the state water utility ECAPAG, which also regulates it under the concession contract; it began operating in Guayaquil in 1999. It was owned jointly at the start by Bechtel Corporation of the US, United Utilities of the UK and Edison of Italy; Bechtel sold the majority of its shares to Proactiva Medio Ambiente in mid-2008, and it is now jointly owned by Proactiva as majority shareholder, the Ecuadorian firm Hidalgo e Hidalgo and the Colombian firm Fanalca.

Inversiones Los Pinares (formerly Emco M.desc: A mining company in Honduras that holds two iron oxide mining licences, ASP and ASP2, and belongs to the EMCO Group, whose main partners are the married couple Lenir Perez and Ana Facusse. The group created a separate firm, Inversiones ECOTEK S.A., to handle iron processing, and the steel company Nucor took part through two Panamanian firms, NE Holdings Subsidiary from March 2015 and NE Holdings from August 2016, saying it ended its ties and sold its NE Holdings shares in October 2019. No published revenue or employee figure was found.

Irish Water.desc: Ireland's publicly owned, regulated, commercial state body responsible for water and wastewater services: it supplies drinking water and collects and treats wastewater. Uisce Eireann became a stand-alone legal entity on 1 January 2023, the date on which Irish Water transitioned to the name Uisce Eireann; in 2023 it had an average of 1,478 employees and served more than 1.6 million domestic and more than 0.2 million non-domestic customers.

Italian-Thai Development Plc (ITD).desc: A Thai engineering and construction company established in 1958 by Dr Chaijudh Karnasuta and Giorgio Berlingieri, listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in 1994, with the Karnasuta family owning a 24% stake as of January 2023. It does a broad range of civil construction work, including buildings, industrial plants, pipelines, railways, expressways, airports, seaports, power plants, hydro-electric dams and mines, and reported revenues of THB52.6 billion in the first nine months of 2023.

Ivanhoe Mines.desc: A mining, development and exploration company continued under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) on 11 September 2012, with its registered office in Vancouver and an African head office in Sandton, Johannesburg; its Class A shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange as IVN and on the OTCQX as IVPAF. Its main assets are the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex, the Kipushi Mine and the Western Forelands exploration project in DR Congo and the Platreef Mine in South Africa, and it had approximately 1,868 employees as at 31 December 2025, excluding employees of the Kamoa-Kakula joint venture.

Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.desc: A mining, development and exploration company continued under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) on 11 September 2012, with its registered office in Vancouver and an African head office in Sandton, Johannesburg; its Class A shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange as IVN and on the OTCQX as IVPAF. Its main assets are the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex, the Kipushi Mine and the Western Forelands exploration project in DR Congo and the Platreef Mine in South Africa, and it had approximately 1,868 employees as at 31 December 2025, excluding employees of the Kamoa-Kakula joint venture.

Ivanplats (Pty) Ltd.desc: The company that holds the Platreef mining rights on the Turfspruit and Macalacaskop properties, which make up the Platreef Mine near Mokopane in South Africa's Limpopo Province, producing platinum, palladium, nickel, rhodium, copper and gold. Ivanhoe Mines holds a 64% interest in the Platreef Mine through Ivanplats; South African beneficiaries of a broad-based black economic empowerment structure hold a combined 26%, and a Japanese consortium of ITOCHU Corporation, the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security and JGC Holdings Corporation holds the remaining 10%.

sources.title: Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2025

J-Power (Electric Power Development Co.).desc: A Japanese electricity generation group that runs hydro, coal-fired, wind and other power plants, sells wholesale power, and holds overseas power projects; it was set up in September 1952 as a government-invested stock company under Japan's Electric Power Development Promotion Act. Group revenue was 1,257.9 billion yen with 7,083 employees in the year to March 2024.

JBS.desc: A Brazilian meat processing company with its head address in Sao Paulo that handles beef, pork and chicken and beneficially owns approximately 83% of the US poultry firm Pilgrim's Pride. Its ultimate controlling shareholders are the brothers Joesley and Wesley Batista, and its direct controlling shareholders are J&F and JBS Participacoes; net revenue was US$82.8 billion in 2024 and it had approximately 280,000 employees worldwide as of 31 December 2024.

JBS reports US$82.8B in net revenue for year FY2024

JISCO.desc: Jiuquan Iron and Steel Corporation is a Chinese steel enterprise in Jiayuguan city, Gansu province, founded in 1958 as the fourth steel industrial base planned by China after Anshan, Wuhan and Baotou; it makes carbon steel and stainless steel and is also one of China's largest aluminium enterprises, with annual capacity reported in 2023 as 12 million tonnes of steel, 1.2 million tonnes of stainless steel and 1.75 million tonnes of electrolytic aluminium. On 19 July 2016 it signed an interest purchase agreement for the Alpart alumina refinery in Jamaica, negotiated with the Russian alumina firm UC Rusal, which had operated the refinery.

JP Autoceste FBiH (Motorways of the Fede.desc: A public company with its headquarters in Mostar and an operational office in Sarajevo, whose main task is the construction, operation and maintenance of motorways and highways in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including organising the toll collection system. It was registered at the Municipal Court in Mostar under number Tt-O-852/10 on 28 October 2010 in accordance with the Law on Roads of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, commenced operations on 1 January 2011, and was established as the legal successor of the Federal Directorate for the Construction, Operation and Maintenance of Motorways.

JP Autoputevi Republike Srpske.desc: A public company based in Banja Luka, established with the aim of managing highways and expressways in the Republic of Srpska, which it also builds, and which handles toll collection at six toll stations: Jakupovci, Catrnja, Kladari, Prnjavor, Laktasi and Kostajnica. The Government of the Republic of Srpska established it by Decision No. 04/1-012-2323/06, adopted at its session held on 10 November 2006.

sources.title: About RS Motorways

Jamuna Multipurpose Bridge Authority (JM.desc: A Bangladeshi body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, created by the Bangladesh Bridge Authority Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. XXXIV of 1985) of 4 July 1985, with its head office in Dhaka, to carry out feasibility studies, planning and implementation for bridges and toll roads, to administer, manage, operate and maintain them, and to provide for the control, regulation and safety of traffic and vehicles on them. The words 'Bangladesh Bridge Authority' were substituted for 'Jamuna Multipurpose Bridge Authority' with effect from 18 December 2007, and the 1985 Ordinance has been repealed by the Bangladesh Bridge Authority Act, 2016.

Jiangsu Delong Nickel Industry Co..desc: A Chinese company founded in 2010 that specialises in the production and sale of nickel alloys and runs a fully integrated production chain from ironmaking and steelmaking through rolling, solution acid pickling and cold rolling; it has been described as the world's second-largest stainless steel supplier after Tsingshan Group and ranked 47th on the 2023 list of China's Top 500 Private Enterprises. It filed for bankruptcy restructuring in July 2024, and as of December 2024 its 28 affiliated companies had declared debts totalling 71.763 billion yuan against reorganizable assets of 10.492 billion yuan.

sources.title: The Rise and Fall of Jiangsu Delong

Johnson Controls.desc: Johnson Controls International plc is a building-technology company incorporated in Ireland and headquartered in Cork; it makes and services heating and cooling, building controls, security, and fire detection and suppression systems. It had about 94,000 people worldwide as of 30 September 2024, and in 2019 it closed the sale of its Power Solutions business.

sources.title: Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024

Junefield Mineral Resources Holdings.desc: A Chinese mineral exploration and development company whose activities include mine prospecting, exploration, mine development and production, with operations in Peru and Ecuador and mining, contracting, gold, iron ore, silver and coal interests in China. No audited size figure or shareholder list was found on an accessible source.

sources.title: Junefield Mineral Resources Holdings Ltd. company profile

KANN Consortium.desc: An investor group that was the major shareholder of the Abuja Electricity Distribution Company with 60 per cent equity, bought with an acquisition loan from United Bank for Africa during Nigeria's 2013 power privatisation. It was unable to service the debt; UBA forced a management change following a court order over the default and took over the obligor's shares in the distribution company, with the Bureau of Public Enterprises acting as receiver/manager and the regulator endorsing the change in shareholding and the appointment of interim management, as reported in December 2021. Its own shareholders are not named in accessible sources.

sources.title: AEDC: How KANN Consortium lost its majority stake to UBA

KEPCO SPC Power Corporation.desc: A Philippine power company described as a joint venture between Korea Electric Power Corporation and SPC Power, formed to build and run a 200 MW coal-fired power plant in Naga City at an estimated cost of $270 million, with the first 100 MW unit expected to be available by February 2011 and the second in May of the same year. Its financing was to come from the Export-Import Bank of Korea, the Asian Development Bank and a syndicate of banks led by Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation.

sources.title: The Philippines' SPC Power agrees financing for 200 MW Naga City coal plant

Kajima Corporation.desc: A Japanese engineering and construction company founded in 1840 and headquartered in Minato, Japan, trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange under ticker 1812. It engages in civil engineering, building construction, real estate development, architectural and civil engineering design and engineering, and is involved in the construction of power stations, railways, roads, airports and seaports.

sources.title: Kajima Corporation (TYO:1812) company profile

Kalsaka Mining SA (KMSA) and Sega Mining.desc: Subsidiaries of Amara Mining, an AIM-listed West Africa-focused gold mining company; the local companies are named Kalsaka Mining SA (KMSA) and Seguenega Mining SA (SMSA), SMSA being described as Amara's local subsidiary in Burkina Faso. Mining at the Kalsaka/Sega gold mine was halted, as announced on 6 August 2014, and SMSA chose to start liquidation after the mining contractor BCM International served a default notice, which Amara said accelerated a closure it had already planned for the fourth quarter.

Kalumbila Minerals (First Quantum Minera.desc: First Quantum Minerals Ltd was incorporated in British Columbia on 21 December 1983, has its head office in Toronto and is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange as FM; it explores for and produces copper, gold and nickel, with copper its primary product. It produced 431,004 tonnes of copper in 2024 and had 14,484 employees and 12,414 sub-contractors at the end of that year.

Kamoa Copper SA.desc: The company that holds the Kamoa-Kakula Copper Complex in Lualaba Province, DR Congo. The DRC government holds a 20% interest in Kamoa Copper; the remaining 80% of Kamoa-Kakula is held indirectly through Kamoa Holding, in which Ivanhoe Mines holds 49.5%, Zijin Mining holds 49.5% through Gold Mountains and the privately owned Crystal River holds 1%. Its Phase 1, 2 and 3 concentrators produced 388,841 tonnes of copper in concentrate in 2025, and Kamoa-Kakula had approximately 7,437 employees at the end of that year.

Karachaganak Petroleum Operating (KPO).desc: An oil and gas exploration and production company incorporated in the Netherlands in 1998 that operates, through its Kazakhstan branch, the Karachaganak oil and gas condensate field in the West Kazakhstan region on behalf of its parent companies, under a Final Production Sharing Agreement signed between those parents and the Government of Kazakhstan. Its parent companies are Shell, Eni, Chevron, Lukoil and KazMunayGas.

Karuturi Global Ltd.desc: A cut-flower business, reported as Karuturi Limited and part of the Karuturi Group, whose chairman and managing director is Sai Ramakrishna Karuturi; it is described as the world's biggest producer of cut roses, with farms in Kenya, Ethiopia and India, and company sources put production at 580 million roses every year. Its Naivasha-based flower farm in Kenya was placed under receivership, with Kieran Day and Ian Small appointed receiver managers through The Business Advisory Group, with salaries three months in arrears; the group's Bangalore subsidiary was reported to be in the red for at least Sh400 million owed to CFC Stanbic Bank plus other creditors.
